correctness.rationale: For all n>=0, x>0 use r=I_{n+1}(x)/I_n(x), a=n+1, q=x/(x+a); the Bessel recurrence gives H_n=2I_n[1-(1+a/x)r], hence sign H_n=-sign(r-q). Riccati r'=1-(2a-1)r/x-r² yields at each contact (r-q)'=(x-a²)/(x+a)². The near-zero series makes r-q<0; contact at x=a² has positive second derivative, so no first contact at or below a². Above a² every zero is an upward transversal crossing, hence at most one. The known Amos-type lower barrier L=x/(a-1/2+sqrt(x²+(a+1/2)²)) satisfies a strict differential subsolution inequality and r-L>0 for x small; at x=a(a+1), L=q, forcing the unique root in (a²,a(a+1)). This gives positive-to-negative sign and disjoint root brackets. b_n=I_n-I_{n+1}>0 and H_n=b_n-b_{n+1}, yielding unique unimodal discrete maximizer between consecutive switches and a two-way adjacent tie only at switches. Discrete heat kernel exp(-2t)I_|k|(2t) makes the ℓ¹→ℓ∞ convolution norm the largest absolute kernel difference. Independent symbolic checks reproduce Riccati contact and lower-barrier small-x coefficient; independent high-precision roots for n=0..12 lie in open intervals with correct signs.
